subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction and memoryFlush work so foreground session messages can run while maintenance is active, and which session-ordering semantics should that preserve?
rationale: The bug is real from source and logs, but the durable fix changes scheduler/session-state behavior rather than a narrow local condition.

options.title: Dedicated maintenance lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a bounded background lane with explicit session-state adoption rules and foreground user-message recovery behavior.

options.title: Watchdog-only recovery
options.body: Keep current serial ordering but make diagnostics cancel or release stuck compaction faster and surface a user-visible recovery notice.

options.title: Keep current ordering
options.body: Accept that compaction may block a session until timeout/recovery and document timeout tuning as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Dedicated maintenance lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a bounded background lane with explicit session-state adoption rules and foreground user-message recovery behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-line ownership and repeated compaction/session work make this the best available routing candidate for the scheduler direction call.
